# openprovider_domain_restore (Resource)

Restores a domain that has expired, where the registry and the API allow it, and charges the account for it (`data.openprovider_domain_price` with `operation = "restore"` shows the price). The restore occurs when Terraform creates or replaces the resource; a change of an attribute that the configuration sets replaces the resource, so use `triggers` to restore again. The apply fails when the account has no such domain, or when the API refuses the restore, for example because the domain is not expired or can no longer be recovered. The deletion of the resource does not change the domain.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# What the restore costs.
data "openprovider_domain_price" "restore" {
  domain    = "example.com"
  operation = "restore"
}

# Restore example.com, once. The account is charged.
resource "openprovider_domain_restore" "example" {
  domain = "example.com"

  # Change a value to restore again.
  triggers = {
    restore = "2026-11"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `domain` (String) The domain name (e.g., example.com).

### Optional

- `triggers` (Map of String) Arbitrary values. A change of a value restores the domain again.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The domain name.
- `status` (String) The status that OpenProvider answered the restore with.
